claim: CCL: separator serialization of chronological alternating-source contexts is not context-free
candidate_status: unverified; two independent nonconstructor whole audits required

obligations.check: Exact definition of chronological pairs for every finite source prefix, empty included, and distinction from physical reversal and history encodings.
Regular slice has four positive even runs with unique exponents and one separator.
First min(A,C)-1 source pairs forced; final initial-run pair exception retained.
A<C fails for either choice of the last first-tape zero's following one; even run gaps and B>=2 used.
A>C fails even though one further zero can be consumed; at least two residual zeros prevent any next one.
A=C forces the last first-stage one to come from the second tape.
Remaining opposite runs force cross-tape pairs, B=D; unequal positive even gaps cannot end with one extra source zero.
Explicit routing (LR)^A(RL)^B proves all required equal-exponent words are present.
Pumping witness lies in the exact slice and uses blocks of length 2P, P>=1.
Every pumping window of length at most P misses at least one member of each matching nonadjacent block pair.
Separator in a pumped substring duplicates it; separator in the unpumped middle causes no omitted case.
If pumped word retains run form and parity, some enlarged block has an unchanged matching block; possible block-order failures already suffice.
Context-free pumping lemma and closure under regular intersection used in their correct directions and quantifiers.
Accepted chronological routing dictionary is the only project premise; source hardness is context, not a fixed-two-tape theorem.
No conclusion about canonical histories, original output context-freeness, all encodings, algebraicity, exact lambda or novelty.
